votes.shortTitle: Laken Riley Act — final passage
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The Laken Riley Act requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain undocumented immigrants who are arrested, charged, or convicted for theft, burglary, or certain violent crimes. It also allows state attorneys general to sue the federal government over certain immigration enforcement decisions.

votes.shortTitle: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The bill funded the federal government through the remainder of fiscal year 2025, largely at prior-year spending levels, averting a shutdown ahead of a March 14 deadline. It also extended several expiring health and other program authorizations.

votes.shortTitle: SAVE Act — proof-of-citizenship voter registration
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The SAVE Act would require individuals to provide documentary proof of U.S. citizenship in person when registering to vote in federal elections. It also directs states to establish procedures to remove noncitizens identified on voter rolls.

votes.shortTitle: One Big Beautiful Bill Act — House passage
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: H.R. 1 extends and modifies the 2017 individual and business tax cuts, creates new deductions for tips and overtime pay, and increases spending on border security and defense. It also reduces projected spending on Medicaid and food-assistance programs and adds new work requirements for some recipients.

votes.shortTitle: Rescissions Act of 2025
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The Rescissions Act canceled about $9 billion in previously approved federal spending, mostly for foreign aid programs and for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. It was the first rescissions package Congress had approved in decades.

votes.shortTitle: One Big Beautiful Bill Act — final passage
votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment
votes.summary: H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, extends and expands the 2017 tax cuts, adds new deductions for tips, overtime pay, and seniors, and raises the cap on state and local tax deductions. It increases border security and defense spending while cutting projected Medicaid and SNAP spending and adding new work requirements; President Trump signed it into law on July 4, 2025.

votes.shortTitle: CLARITY Act — digital asset market structure
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The CLARITY Act creates a regulatory framework dividing oversight of digital assets between the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. It sets registration and disclosure requirements for cryptocurrency exchanges and other digital-asset intermediaries.

votes.shortTitle: GENIUS Act — stablecoin regulation
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The GENIUS Act creates a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, requiring issuers to hold reserves backing their tokens on a one-to-one basis and to comply with new disclosure and licensing rules. It was the first major piece of cryptocurrency legislation enacted into federal law.

votes.shortTitle: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 — shutdown-ending vote
votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment
votes.summary: The bill reopened the federal government after a 43-day shutdown by funding most agencies through January 30, 2026, and providing full-year funding for a smaller group of agencies through September 2026. It also reversed shutdown-related federal layoffs and funded SNAP benefits retroactively.

votes.shortTitle: Epstein Files Transparency Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
votes.summary: The bill directs the Department of Justice to publicly release its investigative files related to Jeffrey Epstein within 30 days, while allowing redactions to protect victim identities, ongoing investigations, and law enforcement techniques. It passed with near-unanimous support.

votes.shortTitle: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 — final passage
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The fiscal year 2026 NDAA authorizes roughly $900 billion in defense spending, including a pay raise for service members and funding for shipbuilding, munitions, and missile-defense programs. It also sets policy on military personnel, procurement, and other Defense Department programs for the year.

votes.shortTitle: War Powers Resolution on Venezuela
votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution
votes.summary: The resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities in or against Venezuela that Congress had not authorized. It failed after U.S. military strikes on suspected drug-trafficking vessels off Venezuela had raised questions in Congress about the administration's legal authority for military action in the region.

votes.shortTitle: Breaking the Gridlock Act — ACA subsidy extension
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The bill extends for additional years the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits that were expanded in 2021 and had lapsed at the end of 2025, lowering health-insurance premiums for people who buy coverage on ACA marketplaces. It passed with support from nearly all Democrats and a small group of Republicans.

votes.shortTitle: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 — full-year government funding
votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments
votes.summary: The bill provides full-year discretionary appropriations for federal agencies for the remainder of fiscal year 2026, replacing the stopgap funding enacted after the fall 2025 shutdown. It sets spending levels across defense and non-defense programs through September 2026.

votes.shortTitle: Resolution disapproving tariffs on Canada
votes.question: On Passage
votes.summary: The resolution terminates the national emergency the President declared in February 2025 to justify a 25 percent tariff on imports from Canada, ending that tariff if it becomes law. It passed with a bipartisan majority, including several Republicans who broke with the administration on trade policy.

votes.shortTitle: War Powers Resolution directing removal of forces from Iran hostilities
votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution
votes.summary: The resolution directs the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran that Congress has not authorized, invoking the War Powers Resolution. It passed the House with support from Democrats and a number of Republicans.

votes.shortTitle: Laken Riley Act — Senate passage
votes.question: On Passage of the Bill
votes.summary: The Laken Riley Act requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain undocumented immigrants who are arrested, charged, or convicted for theft, burglary, or certain violent crimes. It also allows state attorneys general to sue the federal government over certain immigration enforcement decisions.

votes.shortTitle: Confirmation of Pete Hegseth as Secretary of Defense
votes.question: On the Nomination
votes.summary: The Senate confirmed Pete Hegseth, a former Fox News host and Army National Guard officer, to serve as Secretary of Defense. Vice President JD Vance cast the tie-breaking vote after three Republican senators joined all Democrats in voting against the nomination.

votes.shortTitle: Confirmation of Pamela Bondi as Attorney General
votes.question: On the Nomination
votes.summary: The Senate confirmed Pamela Bondi, Florida's former attorney general, to serve as U.S. Attorney General, leading the Justice Department. The vote fell largely along party lines.

votes.shortTitle: Confirmation of Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as HHS Secretary
votes.question: On the Nomination
votes.summary: The Senate confirmed Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to serve as Secretary of Health and Human Services, overseeing federal health, food-safety, and drug-regulatory agencies. Senator Mitch McConnell was the only Republican to vote against the nomination.

votes.shortTitle: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025 — Senate passage
votes.question: On Passage of the Bill
votes.summary: The bill funded the federal government through the remainder of fiscal year 2025, largely at prior-year spending levels, averting a shutdown. It also extended several expiring health and other program authorizations.

votes.shortTitle: Resolution to end the global tariff emergency
votes.question: On the Joint Resolution
votes.summary: S.J.Res. 49 would have terminated the national emergency the President declared in April 2025 to impose broad tariffs on imports from most U.S. trading partners. The resolution failed on a tied 49-49 vote.

votes.shortTitle: GENIUS Act — Senate passage
votes.question: On Passage of the Bill
votes.summary: The GENIUS Act creates a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, requiring issuers to hold reserves backing their tokens on a one-to-one basis and comply with new disclosure and licensing rules. It was the first major piece of cryptocurrency legislation to clear Congress.

votes.shortTitle: War Powers Resolution on Iran — motion to discharge
votes.question: On the Motion to Discharge
votes.summary: S.J.Res. 59 would have directed the President to end U.S. military hostilities against Iran that Congress had not authorized, following U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities earlier that month. A motion to discharge the resolution from committee failed, preventing a vote on final passage.

votes.shortTitle: One Big Beautiful Bill Act — Senate passage
votes.question: On Passage of the Bill
votes.summary: H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, extends and expands the 2017 tax cuts, adds new deductions for tips, overtime pay, and seniors, and increases border security and defense spending. It reduces projected Medicaid and SNAP spending and adds new work requirements; Vice President Vance cast the tie-breaking vote.

votes.shortTitle: Resolution to end the global tariff emergency
votes.question: On the Joint Resolution
votes.summary: S.J.Res. 88 terminates the national emergency the President used to impose broad tariffs on imports from most countries under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Unlike an earlier April 2025 attempt, this resolution passed the Senate, though it still required House and presidential action to take effect.

votes.shortTitle: War Powers Resolution on Venezuela — motion to discharge
votes.question: On the Motion to Discharge
votes.summary: S.J.Res. 90 would have directed the President to end military hostilities within or against Venezuela that Congress had not authorized, after U.S. strikes on suspected drug-trafficking vessels in the region. A motion to discharge the resolution from committee failed, blocking a vote on final passage.

votes.summary: The bill reopened the federal government after a 43-day shutdown by funding most agencies through January 30, 2026, and providing full-year funding for a smaller group of agencies through September 2026. Eight members of the Democratic caucus joined nearly all Republicans to pass it.
